2608.14745.title: Trimer Thouless Pump: Topology, Symmetries, and Multigap Structure
2608.14745.summary:
- Introduces a minimal three‑band “Trimer Thouless Pump” exhibiting multigap topological transport.
- Shows quantized charge pumped via Berry‑curvature hotspots at Dirac‑like avoided crossings, with the middle band mediating flux exchange while having zero net Chern number.
- Maps phase diagram versus central‑site detuning, predicts band‑selective topological invariant transfer, and proposes ultracold‑atom realization in optical superlattices.

2608.14775.title: Spectral preservation under momentum-dependent similarity transformations in non-Hermitian lattice systems
2608.14775.summary:
- Momentum‑dependent similarity transforms preserve spectra in finite non‑Hermitian lattices only under specific conditions.
- For traceless \(2\times2\) Hamiltonians, necessary and sufficient criteria for skew‑diagonalization via constant similarity transforms are derived, with explicit matrices.
- Bulk spectral preservation requires the generalized Brillouin zone to lie inside the smallest zero of \(\det S(z)\) and no critical non‑Hermitian skin effect; two‑sidedness of \(S(z)\) only alters a finite number of boundary eigenvalues.

2608.14784.title: No-Go Theorem and Routes towards Cavity-Enhanced Superconductivity
2608.14784.summary:
- Minimal cavity electrodynamics yields a no‑go theorem: vacuum fluctuations suppress superconductivity because paramagnetic exchange cannot outweigh diamagnetic renormalization.
- Enhancement is possible only by coupling an additional collective mode that boosts paramagnetic attraction or by weakening a competing order that limits superconductivity.
- Thus, practical cavity‑enhanced superconductivity requires an extra cavity‑coupled material degree of freedom to overcome the inherent suppression.

2608.14805.title: Interaction driven charge transfer transitions in closely spaced graphene double layers
2608.14805.summary:
- Charge transfer in graphene double layers proceeds through interaction‑driven phase transitions, not simple electrostatics.
- Intralayer exchange causes abrupt subband transfer, while interlayer exchange stabilizes coherent intermediate phases for gradual transfer.
- The process reconstructs the quasiparticle spectrum, making interlayer tunneling a probe of bias‑dependent interacting systems.

2608.14810.title: Electronic structure and magnetic correlations in the epitaxially strained bilayer nickelate La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_{7}$
2608.14810.summary:
- Orbital‑selective renormalization of Ni 3d states in La₃Ni₂O₇, with strong incoherence and proximity to localization.
- In‑plane strain (tensile or moderate compressive ≤ –2 %) boosts magnetic correlations; large compressive strain (~–4 %) induces a Lifshitz transition that removes the γ Fermi‑surface sheet and suppresses magnetism.
- Results support a spin‑ and charge‑density‑wave stripe instability driven by Fermi‑surface nesting, tunable by pressure or strain.

2608.14842.title: Rapid supercurrent decay in Mn$_5$Si$_3$ Josephson junctions
2608.14842.summary:
- Ic decays exponentially with ξ ≈ 31 nm, far shorter than in FeMn, Cr, NiMn junctions.
- No 0‑π transition detected; Ic(T) for a 1 nm barrier is smooth and monotonic.
- Rapid decay and barrier microstructure limit observable transitions; oriented crystalline barriers are required.

2608.14850.title: Exact Thermoelectric Transport Coefficients and Figure of Merit for Graphene Photothermoelectric Devices from a Finite Zeta-Function Mott Series
2608.14850.summary:
- Finite zeta‑function Mott series yields exact thermoelectric coefficients for polynomial transport functions.
- Applied to graphene photothermoelectric devices (quadratic conductivity) gives closed‑form Seebeck, Lorenz ratio, and figure‑of‑merit, revealing a Seebeck peak and strong Wiedemann–Franz violation at higher temperatures.
- Disorder reduces performance and imposes an upper limit on the electronic figure of merit; radiative heat transport further affects the figure of merit.

2608.14853.title: Physics-Informed Symbolic Regression for Predicting the Glass Transition Temperature of Alkali Borate Glasses
2608.14853.summary:
- Physics‑informed symbolic regression yields a closed‑form Tg model for alkali borate glasses with 14–16 K RMSE.
- Using Rigid Unit Packing Fraction (RUPF) instead of Atomic Packing Fraction captures Tg–dissociation energy–packing interplay and avoids over‑rigidity at intermediate compositions.
- Fitted dissociation energies agree with the Makishima‑Mackenzie model; Monte‑Carlo uncertainty peaks near the boron anomaly region.

2608.14875.title: When do machine-learned exchange-correlation improvements inherit into density-functional tight binding?
2608.14875.summary:
- ML exchange‑correlation functionals lower band‑gap errors at near‑semilocal cost, yet their gains do not transfer to DFTB parameterization because orbital‑dependent GKS operators cannot be exactly represented by a multiplicative potential.
- Transfer‑ratio analysis shows “anti‑transfer” in covalent semiconductors: parent‑level changes move gaps in the wrong direction; the minimal‑basis overgap is dominated by on‑site conventions, largely fixed by correcting the on‑site block and

2608.14880.title: Coherent Phonon Blocking in Superlattices
2608.14880.summary:
- Wave‑mechanics model predicts phonon transmission and thermal resistance in arbitrarily thick superlattices, including all acoustic branches, mode conversion, and incidence angles.
- NSGA‑II genetic algorithm designs bilayers meeting the quarter‑wavelength condition for dominant phonons, yielding up to 3000× higher thermal resistance than previous superlattices.
- Resulting structures enable ultra‑low‑temperature thermal insulation and phonon‑blocking for superconducting flip‑chip assemblies and MEMS/NEMS devices.

2608.14889.title: Antiferroquadrupolar Order in Altermagnetic CoF$_2$
2608.14889.summary:
- Directly observed antiferroquadrupolar charge order in CoF₂ with resonant elastic X‑ray scattering.
- Demonstrated that this quadrupolar order generates the altermagnetic spin‑splitting, linking charge and magnetic degrees of freedom.
- Established resonant X‑ray scattering as a probe for charge multipoles underlying altermagnetism in rutile‑structured materials.

2608.14920.title: Low temperature magnetic structure and lattice response in SmCuAs$_2$
2608.14920.summary:
- XRMS reveals a commensurate antiferromagnetic structure (q = (0,0,) with Sm moments in the ab‑plane and ++–– stacking along c.
- Synchrotron XRD shows tetragonal symmetry down to 8 K; the c‑axis lattice parameter plateaus and rises near T_N, evidencing magnetoelastic coupling.
- Comparison with Pr, Nd, Gd analogues indicates that in‑plane moment orientation, magnetic frustration, and spin‑orbit/magnetoelastic differences govern the low‑temperature resistivity minimum.

2608.15017.title: Quantum Many-Body Scars, Magnon-Pair Condensation, and Hilbert Space Fragmentation in an Anisotropic Heisenberg Model
2608.15017.summary:
- Exact scar eigenstates from RSGA show subextensive entanglement and magnon‑pair condensation with ODLRO.
- At resonance the model maps to a mixed spin‑1/0 XY lattice, decomposing into independent sub‑Hamiltonians.
- Spin‑0 sites act as kinetic constraints, yielding emergent Hilbert‑space fragmentation.

2608.15542.title: Zero-point theorems in quantum many-body physics
2608.15542.summary:
- Extends zero‑point theorems to multi‑parameter Hamiltonian families, revealing inevitable spectral‑gap zeros in quantum spin phase diagrams.
- Relies solely on model‑independent boundary transformation relations, bypassing explicit low‑energy dynamics.
- Presents conjectures that impose universal constraints on relevant operators for critical phenomena in arbitrary dimensions.

2608.15732.title: Accessing Gapped Chiral Phase with Auxiliary-Assisted PEPS
2608.15732.summary:
- Auxiliary-assisted PEPS embed a chiral system with a time‑reversed partner, removing spurious long‑range correlations.
- Resulting states exhibit clean gapped correlations and finite transfer‑matrix correlation lengths for both a Chern insulator and a chiral spin liquid.
- Layer‑resolved momentum projection recovers the universal chiral entanglement spectrum, preserving topological data in the entanglement.

2608.15800.title: Linear response functions from inhomogeneous dynamical mean-field theory
2608.15800.summary:
- Introduces a vertex‑free method for static lattice susceptibilities in inhomogeneous DMFT.
- Uses external field response, bypassing two‑particle vertex calculations.
- Validated on the square‑lattice Hubbard model; matches vertex‑based results and reaches lower temperatures.

2608.15811.title: Topological Altermagnetic Insulators
2608.15811.summary:
- Altermagnetic topological phases emerge in a Lieb lattice with Ising spin‑orbit coupling.
- Quantum spin Hall effect coexists with altermagnetic spin order at fillings 2 and 4 per unit cell.
- Edge modes stay robust against inversion‑symmetry breaking, shaped by edge magnetic structure.

2608.16028.title: Transport-Noise Witnesses of Electronic Multipartite Entanglement
2608.16028.summary:
- Uses equilibrium current‑noise spectrum as a transport‑based witness of multipartite electronic entanglement.
- Derives a basis‑invariant upper bound on integrated, symmetrized noise that signals entanglement.
- Validated on twisted bilayer graphene, MoTe₂, and Hubbard models, detecting entanglement in a fractional Chern insulator.

2608.16219.title: Non-Equilibrium Instantaneous Approximation and Dipole Forbidden d-d Transitions
2608.16219.summary:
- Instantaneous approximation decouples fast relative‑time decay from slow average‑time evolution, enabling efficient non‑equilibrium calculations.
- Coupled with Hubbard‑I DMFT, it embeds driven local dynamics into lattice Green’s functions while retaining momentum resolution.
- Derives an effective coupling for dipole‑forbidden d‑d transitions via d‑p transition plus p‑d hybridization, validated on FePS₃ against time‑resolved photoemission data.
